items.title: With control of Congress, here’s how Democrats could stop Trump’s war in Iran
items.summary: The Democrats’ sweeping victory in the US midterm elections puts them in a stronger position to interfere with President Donald Trump’s agenda. This includes his deeply unpopular and costly war against Iran, which could be among their first priorities. As president, Trump will be able to veto any legislation aimed at ending the war. But the Democrats still have another powerful card up their sleeves: cutting off funding for the war. There are caveats, however. History suggests exercising this power could trigger a political confrontation that may backfire. And even if the Democrats succeed in ending the war, they may not be able to reverse the damage it has done to the US’ global standing. The limits of legislation Democrats will have three main options to try to force the war against Iran to a close. Two of these, however, face significant limitations. The first – and perhaps most obvious – option is through legislation. There are a few different ways to do this. One approach is to pass a resolution calling for an end to the war. items.title: A father’s U-turn, a YouTuber, and a CCTV ‘glitch’: Inside the revival of the Disha Salian case
items.summary: Disha Salian died in June 2020. A young talent manager working in Bollywood, she tragically fell to her death from the 12th storey of a flat in Mumbai on the intervening night of June 8 and 9, 2020. But the claims surrounding the death of the 28-year-old refuse to die. Despite multiple months-long investigations, CCTV and medical evidence, and witness testimonies that categorically state otherwise, the same lurid claims that she was raped, murdered, that she attended a party with high-profile figures, that her death was linked to the suicide of actor Sushant Singh Rajput a few days later and that she was naked when her body was discovered recirculate periodically, on social media and on TV channels. This time, there is a new twist in this already convoluted sequence of events. Satish Salian spent five years after the sudden death of his daughter, Disha, trying his best to quash these rumours. He and his wife, Vasanti, would tell anyone who would listen – family members, friends, neighbours and journalists – that these claims were simply not true. items.title: Authorities can't pass orders blindly based on panel lawyer's legal opinion: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that administrative and statutory authorities cannot pass executive orders blindly, relying solely the legal opinion of their panel advocates. Justice T M Nadaf held that legal opinions given by panel advocates are only advisory in nature and cannot replace the independent decision-making process of the competent authority. The Court added that an authority that merely copies or approves a legal opinion without examining the relevant facts and law abdicates its statutory power and acts under dictation. “ If an authority blindly copies or signs off the order only on the legal opinion, without examining the facts and relevant law by itself, it amounts to an abdication of statutory power and acting under dictation. Such orders require to be held as arbitrary, invalid and lacking jurisdiction ,” the Court said. . He had later gotten bail from the High Court. However, his current plea was filed seeking permission to go abroad, the Court noted. The judge observed that Thachankary had remained in hospital throughout his period in custody. "He has been admitted to the hospital from the date of admission till the date of release.
